title: Clusone to home via Cima Blum, Monte Pare and the Agnelli ridge
terrain: point-to-point, 18.2km, 1534m D+ / 1074m D-, high point 2045m, limestone above 1600m, finishes at the front door

steps.target: Z1-Z2 approach out of Clusone, 55-84% LTHR
Z2-Z3 sustained climb to ~1890m, ~1240m D+ continuous, 84-89% LTHR
Z1-Z2 rolling ridge to the 2045m high point, 55-84% LTHR
Z1-Z2 descent 930m to home, poles, hike anything over 20%, 55-80% LTHR

coachNotes: ROUTE APPROVED, athlete's own GPX, 21 Aug. Clusone 652m to home 1111m, 18.2km, 1534m D+, 1074m D-, high point 2045m. WHY IT IS A YES. Gradient density is 84 m/km against Pirin's 87: this is the closest thing to race terrain available, and the 10km unbroken climb from Clusone to 1890m is the specific rehearsal, because Pirin's 3300m arrives in long sustained ascents and not in fragments. Total descent is 1074m, which is LESS than the 1400m the 3x470m loop design carried, because the route finishes 459m above where it starts. And it ends at the front door: no car to return to, no loop to extend, the endpoint is fixed by geography rather than by discipline. That last point is why this beats the session it replaces. THE ONE DEVIATION, AND IT IS REAL. The descent is 932m in a single continuous bout over 4.7km, averaging -20%, with the final kilometre at -25%. The plan said no bout over 470m. This is double, and it is the steepest, latest, most fatigued braking of the day. It is being accepted rather than waved through, on one argument: this bout is worth more risk today than on 5 September. Today it has three weeks and a flat week 7 behind it, so a band that complains has somewhere to complain. At D-7 it has nothing. Note also that 1011m in one bout is what 2 August already carried without incident, so 932m is not new ground, only new ground after a flat fortnight. THE RULE THAT MAKES IT SAFE: HIKE ANYTHING OVER 20%. That is the whole of the final kilometre and most of km 15-16. Poles from the high point, short steps, cadence 175+, no heel-braking, no let-it-run. This is not caution, it is what you will actually do at hour eight in Pirin, so rehearse it. If you run that last kilometre because it is nearly home, the session failed. WET LIMESTONE ABOVE 1600m. 65-107mm fell Thursday and Friday and the Blum to Pare ridge is limestone. No polished slab, no cable section, no exposed step-down. You know the variants better than any forecast does: if the ridge line is greasy, drop to the lower path and lose the metres. NO BAIL-OUT ABOVE 1800m and the car stays in Clusone. Storm rule inverts because of that: turn back BEFORE the high point, not after. First thunder on the climb and you go back down the way you came. FUELLING, this is the main rehearsal now: eat every 40 minutes from the first climb, race products only, 60-90g carbs per hour, 2 x 500ml minimum. You are out ~4h10, which is your first honest read on hour four. Write down what you actually took. CLIMB EFFORT 84-89% LTHR, not Z3. You will not climb Pirin at Z3, so do not rehearse it here. If the last 300m of climbing is a grind at that effort, that is the session working. AMBER: any lateral knee signal in the first hour and you turn at Monte Pare and take the lower line home, ~800m D+, load 110. Garmin expect 300-360.
